service:
Lambda

Overview

AWS Lambda Core is a set of APIs for managing shared infrastructure resources used by Lambda. The Lambda Core API provides operations for creating and managing network connectors that enable Lambda compute resources to access resources in your Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC).

Network connectors provision elastic network interfaces (ENIs) in your VPC subnets, providing a managed network path from Lambda compute environments to private resources such as Amazon RDS databases, Amazon ElastiCache clusters, and internal APIs. You create a network connector once and attach it to one or more Lambda compute resources at run time.

The Lambda Core API Reference provides information about each of the API methods, including details about the parameters in each API request and response.

You can use Software Development Kits (SDKs), Integrated Development Environment (IDE) Toolkits, and command line tools to access the API. For installation instructions, see Tools for Amazon Web Services.

For a list of Region-specific endpoints that Lambda supports, see Lambda endpoints and quotas in the Amazon Web Services General Reference.

When making the API calls, you will need to authenticate your request by providing a signature. Lambda supports signature version 4. For more information, see Signature Version 4 signing process in the Amazon Web Services General Reference.

operations.CreateNetworkConnector:
Creates a network connector that enables Lambda compute resources to route outbound traffic through your Amazon VPC. The network connector provisions elastic network interfaces (ENIs) in the subnets you specify, providing a managed network path to private resources such as databases, caches, and internal APIs.

This operation is asynchronous. The network connector starts in PENDING state while ENIs are provisioned in your VPC (provisioning typically takes up to 10 minutes). Use GetNetworkConnector to poll the connector state until it reaches ACTIVE. Once active, you can attach the connector to supported Lambda compute resources — such as MicroVMs and WebFunctions — at run time. For how to attach a connector, see the documentation for the specific compute type.

This operation is idempotent when you provide a ClientToken — if you retry a request that completed successfully using the same client token, the operation returns the existing connector without creating a duplicate.
operations.DeleteNetworkConnector:
Initiates deletion of a network connector. The connector transitions to DELETING state while elastic network interfaces are cleaned up asynchronously. After deletion completes, subsequent calls to GetNetworkConnector return ResourceNotFoundException.

This operation is idempotent — calling delete on a connector that is already deleting or has been deleted succeeds without error. You can delete connectors in ACTIVE or FAILED states. Before deleting a connector, ensure that no Lambda compute resources are using it, as they will lose VPC egress connectivity immediately.

Deleting with an unqualified identifier removes the connector and all of its versions. To remove a single historical version, supply its version-qualified ARN; the connector and its remaining versions are unaffected. You can't delete the latest version on its own — delete the connector to remove it.
operations.GetNetworkConnector:
Retrieves the current configuration, state, and metadata of a network connector. The Identifier parameter accepts the connector ID, name, or full ARN. Use this operation to poll connector state after creation or update, or to inspect the current VPC configuration and any failure reasons.

The response includes the full connector configuration, current state, and — if the connector has been updated — the LastUpdateStatus and LastUpdateStatusReasonCode fields that indicate whether the most recent update succeeded or failed.
operations.ListNetworkConnectorVersions:
Returns a paginated list of the versions of a network connector. Each configuration update creates a new immutable version; this operation lists those versions for the connector you specify. You can optionally filter results by version state. Use the Marker parameter from a previous response to retrieve the next page of results.

Each item in the response includes the version-qualified ARN, version number, current state, and last modified timestamp for that version. To retrieve the current (latest) configuration of the connector, use GetNetworkConnector; to inspect a specific version, call GetNetworkConnector with a version-qualified identifier.
operations.ListNetworkConnectors:
Returns a paginated list of network connectors in your account for the current Region. You can optionally filter results by connector state. Use the Marker parameter from a previous response to retrieve the next page of results.

Each item in the response includes the connector ARN, name, ID, type, current state, and last modified timestamp. To retrieve full configuration details for a specific connector, use GetNetworkConnector.
operations.UpdateNetworkConnector:
Updates the VPC configuration or operator role of an existing network connector. You can modify the subnet IDs, security group IDs, network protocol, or operator role. The connector must be in ACTIVE state to accept updates.

This operation is asynchronous. The connector remains in ACTIVE state during the update — existing workloads that reference this connector are not disrupted. Use GetNetworkConnector to monitor the LastUpdateStatus field, which transitions through InProgress to Successful or Failed. If the update fails, the LastUpdateStatusReasonCode field provides a specific error code for troubleshooting. This operation is idempotent when you provide a ClientToken.

Each successful configuration change creates a new immutable version. A connector can have a limited number of versions; once that limit is reached, further updates fail with NetworkConnectorLimitExceededException until you delete older versions.

refs.NetworkConnectorVpcEgressConfiguration$A: The types of Lambda compute resources that can use this connector. Valid values are MicroVm and WebFunction. Specify exactly one value.

refs.CreateNetworkConnectorRequest$ClientToke: A unique, case-sensitive identifier that you provide to ensure the idempotency of the request. If you retry a request with the same client token, the API returns the existing connector without creating a duplicate.
refs.UpdateNetworkConnectorRequest$ClientToke: A unique, case-sensitive identifier to ensure idempotency of the update request.

ComputeResourceType.base: The type of Lambda compute resource that can use a network connector.

refs.GetNetworkConnectorResponse$LastModified: The date and time when the connector configuration was last modified.
refs.NetworkConnectorSummary$LastModified: The date and time when the connector was last modified.
refs.NetworkConnectorVersionSummary$LastModif: The date and time when this connector version was last modified.

InvalidParameterValueException.base: One of the parameters in the request is not valid. Check the error message for details about which parameter failed validation.

refs.ListNetworkConnectorVersionsRequest$MaxI: The maximum number of versions to return per page. Valid range: 1 to 100.
refs.ListNetworkConnectorsRequest$MaxItems: The maximum number of connectors to return per page. Valid range: 1 to 100.

refs.CreateNetworkConnectorResponse$Arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the network connector.
refs.CreateNetworkConnectorResponse$VersionAr: The qualified ARN of the connector version created by this request, including the immutable version suffix.
refs.DeleteNetworkConnectorResponse$Arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the network connector.
refs.DeleteNetworkConnectorResponse$VersionAr: The qualified ARN of the connector version affected by this request, including the immutable version suffix.
refs.GetNetworkConnectorResponse$Arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the network connector.
refs.GetNetworkConnectorResponse$VersionArn: The qualified ARN of the specific connector version returned by this request, including the immutable version suffix. This is populated only when you supply a version-qualified identifier. On a standard (unqualified) request, this field is not populated; the connector's latest active version is returned instead through the LatestVersionArn and LatestVersion fields described below.
refs.GetNetworkConnectorResponse$LatestVersio: The qualified ARN of the connector's latest active version, including the immutable version suffix. This field is returned only on a standard (unqualified) request; when you supply a version-qualified identifier it is not returned, and VersionArn is returned instead.
refs.NetworkConnectorSummary$LatestVersionArn: The qualified ARN of the connector's latest version, including the immutable version suffix.
refs.NetworkConnectorVersionSummary$Arn: The unqualified ARN of the network connector that this version belongs to.
refs.NetworkConnectorVersionSummary$VersionAr: The qualified ARN of this connector version, including the immutable version suffix.
refs.UpdateNetworkConnectorResponse$Arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the network connector.
refs.UpdateNetworkConnectorResponse$VersionAr: The qualified ARN of the connector version resulting from this update, including the immutable version suffix.

NetworkConnectorConfiguration.base: The network configuration for a network connector. Different connector types use different configuration shapes; specify the configuration that matches your connector type.

refs.CreateNetworkConnectorRequest$Configurat: The network configuration for the connector. Specify a VpcEgressConfiguration to enable outbound traffic routing through your VPC.
refs.CreateNetworkConnectorResponse$Configura: The network configuration of the connector, including VPC subnets and security groups.
refs.DeleteNetworkConnectorResponse$Configura: The network configuration of the connector, including VPC subnets and security groups.
refs.GetNetworkConnectorResponse$Configuratio: The network configuration of the connector, including VPC subnets and security groups.
refs.UpdateNetworkConnectorRequest$Configurat: The updated network configuration for the connector. Provide the full VpcEgressConfiguration including all subnet IDs and security group IDs — this replaces the existing configuration.
refs.UpdateNetworkConnectorResponse$Configura: The network configuration of the connector, including VPC subnets and security groups.

NetworkConnectorId.base: The unique identifier for a network connector, assigned by the service at creation time

refs.CreateNetworkConnectorResponse$Id: The unique identifier of the network connector.
refs.DeleteNetworkConnectorResponse$Id: The unique identifier of the network connector.
refs.GetNetworkConnectorResponse$Id: The unique identifier of the network connector.
refs.NetworkConnectorSummary$Id: The unique identifier of the network connector.
refs.NetworkConnectorVersionSummary$Id: The unique identifier of the network connector.
refs.UpdateNetworkConnectorResponse$Id: The unique identifier of the network connector.

NetworkConnectorIdentifier.base: A flexible identifier that accepts a network connector ID, name, or ARN

refs.DeleteNetworkConnectorRequest$Identifier: The identifier of the network connector to delete. Provide an unqualified ARN (or an ID or name) to delete the entire connector and all of its versions, or a version-qualified ARN — one that includes the immutable version suffix — to delete a specific historical version. You can't delete the latest version with a version-qualified identifier; delete the connector instead.
refs.GetNetworkConnectorRequest$Identifier: The identifier of the network connector to retrieve. You can specify the connector ID, name, or ARN. Provide an unqualified ARN (or an ID or name) to retrieve the connector's latest version, or a version-qualified ARN — one that includes the immutable version suffix — to retrieve a specific historical version.
refs.ListNetworkConnectorVersionsRequest$Iden: The identifier of the network connector whose versions you want to list. You can specify the connector ID, name, or full ARN. Specify an unqualified identifier — this operation lists all versions of the connector, not a specific version.
refs.UpdateNetworkConnectorRequest$Identifier: The identifier of the network connector to update. You can specify the connector ID, name, or full ARN.

NetworkConnectorLastUpdateStatus.base: The status of the most recent update operation on a network connector: Successful, Failed, or InProgress.

refs.GetNetworkConnectorResponse$LastUpdateSt: The status of the most recent update operation (Successful, Failed, or InProgress).
refs.UpdateNetworkConnectorResponse$LastUpdat: The status of this update operation (typically InProgress immediately after the call).

refs.GetNetworkConnectorResponse$LastUpdateSt: A human-readable explanation of the last update status.
refs.UpdateNetworkConnectorResponse$LastUpdat: A human-readable explanation of the update status.

NetworkConnectorLastUpdateStatusReasonCo.base: A machine-readable code indicating why the last update operation reached its current status. Use this for programmatic error handling.

refs.GetNetworkConnectorResponse$LastUpdateSt: A machine-readable code indicating the reason for the last update status. Use this for programmatic error handling.

NetworkConnectorLimitExceededException.base: The request would exceed a network connector limit. For CreateNetworkConnector, the account has reached the maximum number of network connectors allowed. For UpdateNetworkConnector, the connector has reached the maximum number of versions allowed.

refs.CreateNetworkConnectorRequest$Name: A unique name for the network connector within your account and Region. You can use the name to identify the connector in subsequent API calls.

refs.CreateNetworkConnectorRequest$OperatorRo: The ARN of the IAM role that Lambda assumes to manage elastic network interfaces in your VPC. This role must have permissions for ec2:CreateNetworkInterface, ec2:DeleteNetworkInterface, and related describe operations.
refs.CreateNetworkConnectorResponse$OperatorR: The ARN of the IAM role that Lambda uses to manage the underlying ENI resources for this connector.
refs.DeleteNetworkConnectorResponse$OperatorR: The ARN of the IAM role that Lambda uses to manage the underlying ENI resources for this connector.
refs.GetNetworkConnectorResponse$OperatorRole: The ARN of the IAM role that Lambda uses to manage the underlying ENI resources for this connector.
refs.UpdateNetworkConnectorRequest$OperatorRo: The updated ARN of the IAM role that Lambda assumes to manage ENIs. Use this to change the operator role without recreating the connector.
refs.UpdateNetworkConnectorResponse$OperatorR: The ARN of the IAM role that Lambda uses to manage the underlying ENI resources for this connector.

refs.NetworkConnectorVpcEgressConfiguration$S: The IDs of the VPC security groups to attach to the ENIs. All security groups must be in the same VPC as the subnets.

NetworkConnectorState.base: The lifecycle state of a network connector. A connector is PENDING while resources provision, ACTIVE when ready for use, INACTIVE when temporarily unavailable, FAILED when creation or update fails, DELETING while resources are cleaned up, and DELETE_FAILED when deletion fails.

refs.CreateNetworkConnectorResponse$State: The current state of the network connector.
refs.DeleteNetworkConnectorResponse$State: The current state of the network connector. The State field is typically DELETING after this call.
refs.GetNetworkConnectorResponse$State: The current state of the network connector.
refs.ListNetworkConnectorVersionsRequest$Stat: Optional filter to return only versions in the specified state (for example, ACTIVE or FAILED).
refs.ListNetworkConnectorsRequest$State: Optional filter to return only connectors in the specified state (for example, ACTIVE or FAILED).
refs.NetworkConnectorSummary$State: The current state of the network connector.
refs.NetworkConnectorVersionSummary$State: The current state of this connector version.
refs.UpdateNetworkConnectorResponse$State: The current state of the network connector.

NetworkConnectorStateReasonCode.base: A machine-readable code indicating why the connector reached its current state. Use this for programmatic error handling.

refs.GetNetworkConnectorResponse$StateReasonC: A machine-readable code indicating the reason for the current state. Use this for programmatic error handling.
refs.NetworkConnectorVersionSummary$StateReas: A machine-readable code indicating the reason for the current state. Use this for programmatic error handling.

refs.NetworkConnectorVpcEgressConfiguration$S: The IDs of the VPC subnets where Lambda provisions elastic network interfaces (ENIs). Specify 1 to 16 subnets. All subnets must be in the same VPC.

NetworkConnectorSummary.base: Summary information about a network connector returned by ListNetworkConnectors. Contains identifying fields and current state. To retrieve full configuration details, use GetNetworkConnector.

refs.CreateNetworkConnectorRequest$Tags: A map of key-value pairs to associate with the network connector for organization, cost allocation, or access control.

NetworkConnectorType.base: The type of a network connector. VPC_EGRESS provides VPC egress connectivity.

refs.CreateNetworkConnectorResponse$Version: The version number assigned to the connector. A newly created connector starts at version 1.
refs.DeleteNetworkConnectorResponse$Version: The version number of the connector version affected by this request.
refs.GetNetworkConnectorResponse$Version: The version number of the network connector. On a standard (unqualified) request, this is the connector's current version; each configuration update increments it. When you supply a version-qualified identifier, this is the specific version you requested.
refs.GetNetworkConnectorResponse$LatestVersio: The version number of the connector's latest active version. Each configuration update creates a new immutable version; this attribute exposes the most recent one. This field is returned only on a standard (unqualified) request.
refs.NetworkConnectorSummary$LatestVersion: The version number of the connector's latest version. Each configuration update creates a new immutable version; this attribute exposes the most recent one.
refs.NetworkConnectorVersionSummary$Version: The version number of this connector version.
refs.UpdateNetworkConnectorResponse$Version: The version number of the connector version resulting from this update. A configuration change creates a new, incremented version; a no-op update returns the current version number.

NetworkConnectorVersionSummary.base: Summary information about a single version of a network connector returned by ListNetworkConnectorVersions. Each configuration update creates a new immutable version; this shape describes one such version. To retrieve the full configuration of a version, call GetNetworkConnector with a version-qualified identifier.

refs.ListNetworkConnectorVersionsResponse$Net: A list of connector version summaries for the current page of results.

NetworkConnectorVpcEgressConfiguration.base: Configuration for a VPC egress network connector. Specifies the VPC subnets, security groups, network protocol, and associated Lambda compute resource types.

refs.NetworkConnectorConfiguration$VpcEgressC: Configuration for a VPC egress network connector. Specifies the subnets, security groups, and network protocol for routing outbound traffic through your VPC.

refs.ListNetworkConnectorsResponse$NetworkCon: A list of network connector summaries for the current page of results.

NetworkProtocol.base: The network protocol for a connector. IPv4 enables IPv4-only networking; DualStack enables both IPv4 and IPv6.

refs.NetworkConnectorVpcEgressConfiguration$N: The network protocol for the connector. Specify IPv4 for IPv4-only networking, or DualStack for both IPv4 and IPv6.

ResourceConflictException.base: The request could not be completed due to a conflict with the current state of the resource. For example, attempting to update a connector that is not in ACTIVE state.

ResourceNotFoundException.base: The specified network connector does not exist. Verify the identifier (ID, name, or ARN) and Region.

ServiceException.base: An internal service error occurred. Retry the request with exponential backoff.

refs.GetNetworkConnectorResponse$StateReason: A human-readable explanation of the current state, populated when the state is FAILED or DELETE_FAILED.
refs.ListNetworkConnectorVersionsRequest$Mark: The pagination token from a previous ListNetworkConnectorVersions response. Use this value to retrieve the next page of results.
refs.ListNetworkConnectorVersionsResponse$Nex: The pagination token to include in a subsequent request to retrieve the next page. This value is null when there are no more results.
refs.ListNetworkConnectorsRequest$Marker: The pagination token from a previous ListNetworkConnectors response. Use this value to retrieve the next page of results.
refs.ListNetworkConnectorsResponse$NextMarker: The pagination token to include in a subsequent request to retrieve the next page. This value is null when there are no more results.
refs.NetworkConnectorLimitExceededException$m: The account has reached the maximum number of network connectors allowed.
refs.NetworkConnectorVersionSummary$StateReas: A human-readable explanation of the current state, populated when the state is FAILED.
refs.TooManyRequestsException$retryAfterSecon: The number of seconds to wait before retrying the request.

TooManyRequestsException.base: The request was throttled due to exceeding the allowed request rate. Retry the request after a brief wait using exponential backoff.
